evidence: PATHS: The brief names /instructions/hireops_rules.md and /instructions/integration.md (instruction.md:11) and /assets/seed_data.json (instruction.md:13); all three exist under task/environment/ and are staged by environment/Dockerfile:14-16 (COPY instructions/ /instructions/; COPY assets/ /assets/; chmod -R a+rX). The Dockerfile is byte-identical (CRLF-normalised) to the frozen template; integration.md equals the template plus one appended symlink paragraph (lines 16-19). task.toml:2 artifacts=["/app","/assets"] per contract. seed_data.json parses as JSON. CONTENT vs PROMPT/RULES: seed users = exactly the 7 staff + 3 candidates listed in instruction.md:17 with matching roles (3 recruiter, 3 hiring_manager, 1 observer, 3 candidate); no passwords in the seed (password only in brief, as profile expects). hireops_rules.md:204-209 promises people, three jobs with ordered cards, messages with one long conversation, a few notes, read markers counted from the first message, candidate wording and page size 30: seed has 3 jobs, 16 applications with contiguous 1-based positions per (job,stage), 127 messages (APP-101=120, APP-201=3, APP-301=3, APP-302=1), 3 notes, 6 read markers, thread_page_size=30, candidate_status_labels exactly equal to the rules table at hireops_rules.md:183-190, stages in rules order. interview_limit 3/2/3 within 1..50 and not exceeded (Interview counts 2/1/1). Rejected APP-301 carries rejected_from=SCREEN and reject_reason as rules 3 requires. Every application/sender/author/read id resolves; messages are chronological per conversation in file order with no timestamp ties, so read_count is unambiguous. Candidate accounts own their seeded applications by email (rules:34-36). CONTENT vs JUDGES: functional prompt Z (prompt.md:25) and criterion at judge.toml:407 assume Platform Engineer Applied = Greta Lindqvist, Ade Bello, Marco Rossi and Screen = Priya Nair, Samuel Ortiz: seed APP-105/106/108 positions 1/2/3 APPLIED and APP-103/104 positions 1/2 SCREEN on JOB-PLAT - match. Noor's note 'Strong systems answers; weaker on incident follow-up.' is seed note on APP-101 (Noor, JOB-PLAT) - match. 'Lena starts with 1 unread' (prompt.md:25, judge.toml:335): APP-301 messages REC3,CAN3,REC3 with Lena read_count=2 -> one later message by someone else = 1 - match. app_context.md:29-31 'three jobs; Noor Haddad's Platform Engineer conversation is long (120 messages at the start)' - match (APP-101=120). Tomas's seeded Data Analyst conversation used as fallback in T exists (APP-201). Paging criteria (judge.toml:317,324) state no fixed count, so messages added by other reviews do not break them. CONTENT vs SOLUTION: solution/app/src/seed_data.json is byte-identical to environment/assets/seed_data.json (sha256 a1c65c80...3740 both). db.js:10 reads it beside the module (consistent with instruction.md:15 '/assets ... unavailable at runtime' and rules section 8), seeds once (db.js:62), maps read_count to the read_count-th message id (db.js:82-83) and links candidate accounts by email (db.js:69-74), i.e. the golden consumes the asset exactly as the brief describes. Scripted golden (workspace.json, hash verified; not a judge run) reports 'seeded card order and internal notes are loaded' passed=true. COUNTEREXAMPLE ATTEMPTS: (a) Broken app ignoring read markers shows Lena 3 unread -> caught by hro_unread_counts; app reloading seed on restart -> caught by judge.toml:407. Neither passes because of an asset/judge mismatch. (b) Conforming alternative: an app that orders messages by created_at instead of file order, or treats read_count as a count from the first message per rules:207-208, reaches the same values the judges assume because file order equals chronological order with no ties; an app that copies the seed into /app as instructed is fully served. No conforming reading of the asset yields a different graded value. No shipped asset is missing or unused. LIMITS: this is static content verification plus a hash-verified scripted golden; no configured judge run was observed for this row, but the row's question (asset presence and content agreement) is answered by the bytes themselves.
